_meta: A token embedding vector and a positional-encoding vector, used to show why the Transformer multiplies token embeddings by sqrt(d_model) before adding positional encodings. In the original Transformer, the input to the first layer is (token embedding) + (positional encoding). Token embeddings are typically initialized small -- each component around 1/sqrt(d_model) -- so the embedding vector's norm is about 1. Sinusoidal positional encodings, by contrast, have components in [-1, 1], so their vector norm grows with dimension (about sqrt(d_model/2) or larger). Without scaling, the positional signal therefore DOMINATES the sum and the actual token identity is a small perturbation on top of a large positional vector -- the model can barely tell the tokens apart. Multiplying the token embedding by sqrt(d_model) raises its norm to about sqrt(d_model), making it COMPARABLE to the positional encoding's norm, so token identity and position contribute on equal footing. d_model is the model dimension (4 here); embedding is a token embedding with each component 1/sqrt(4)=0.5 (norm 1.0); positional is a positional-encoding vector with norm 2.0. The scale is sqrt(d_model)=2, which raises the embedding norm to 2.0 -- equal to the positional norm. d_model, embedding, and positional are the fixture; the scale factor, the scaled embedding, and every norm and ratio are computed.
